class.name: NetwAction
class.brief_description: A predicted discrete action bound to one authority method.

method.name: request
method.description: Requests the server authority method for [param view_tick], carrying [param data] as its second argument. The local controller gets an immediate [member predict] effect. Non-owning peers do nothing, so server consume and remote display passes cannot double fire a command. [b]Player request.[/b]

members.member: Confirms the optimistic effect, taking the ghost [Node] [member predict] returned. Unset, the ghost is freed with [method Node.queue_free].
Creates the local optimistic effect and returns the ghost [Node] that [member confirm] and [member revert] later receive.
Reverts the optimistic effect, taking the ghost [Node] [member predict] returned. Unset, the ghost is freed with [method Node.queue_free].
Ticks before an unresolved request reverts. [code]0[/code] derives a conservative default from the lag-compensation engine.
The server execution policy. Defaults to [constant TIMING_IMMEDIATE], which is arrival-time execution with no readiness assumptions, so stricter modes are opted into per action.

signal.name: confirmed
signal.description: Emitted when the authoritative result adopts the optimistic effect.

signal.name: denied
signal.description: Emitted when the server denies the optimistic effect or it times out.

constants.constant: Execute on the server when [member NetwActionContext.view_tick] arrives.

Execute after server history records [member NetwActionContext.view_tick]. This mode is owner-anchored. It guarantees only that the action owner's recorded state is ready at the view tick, and gates no other entity, so cross-entity validation must use [method NetwMultiplayer.lagcomp_sample] or [method NetwMultiplayer.lagcomp_rewind] for those targets. Determinism is a precondition, not a toggle. The placement agrees with the client only when consuming the same input yields the same state, and resolution is deferred until that state exists, so remote peers see the result later. Use [constant TIMING_IMMEDIATE] when the action must not wait. Under loss, the consume policy may fill a missing input slot: this mode guarantees a recorded state exists, not that it came from the real input.
Execute as soon as the request reaches the server.
